heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb as referred to in Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, and Integrated Service Center.
10. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
11. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
12. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
13. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
14. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
15. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
16. Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children hereinafter referred to as KPK2BGA is the Commission for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency established by the Regent which is a non-structural commission.
17. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
18. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

translated_text:
CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Institutions

heading: Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by:
a. Integrated Services; and
b. KPK2BGA.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Integrated Services

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

1. Integrated services as referred to in Article 6 letter a are established by the Regional Government in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
2. The establishment of integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of members from regional government elements, non-governmental organizations, health service institutions, law enforcement apparatus, professional personnel, volunteer companions, social workers, religious leaders, safe houses (shelters), and social rehabilitation centers.

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

The duties of integrated services as referred to in Article 7 are to pursue prevention, recovery and social reintegration, provide legal protection, conduct coordination and, pursue increased community participation, as well as monitoring and reporting.

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Prevention Efforts

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 8 include:
a. organizing communication, information, and education about gender-based violence and children;
b. socialization of laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and children.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Recovery and Social Reintegration Efforts

heading: Article 10
Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Legal Protection

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

Legal protection as referred to in Article 8 includes:
a. providing protection in safe houses (shelters);
b. providing assistance in legal proceedings at the high court level; and
c. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence which may be carried out through guardianship appointment in accordance with applicable regulations.

heading: Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Coordination and Cooperation

heading: Article 12
Paragraph 5
translated_text:
Paragraph 5

Community Participation Enhancement Efforts

heading: Article 13
Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 8 include monitoring, documentation and reporting of gender-based violence and child cases.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

The implementation of integrated services is coordinated by the Regional Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

KPK2BGA

Article 16

1. KPK2BGA as referred to in Article 6 letter b, is established by the Regional Government in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
2. The establishment of KPK2BGA as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of members from SKPD responsible for Health affairs, SKPD responsible for Social and Labor affairs, Police, community leaders, religious leaders, non-governmental organization activists, academics, and practitioners.

heading: Article 17
Article 18
Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

The implementation of KPK2BGA is facilitated by the Regional Work Unit responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

The procedures, requirements and establishment of Integrated Services and KPK2BGA are regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Cooperation

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the regional government may cooperate with the Government, other Regional Governments.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration and development of integrated service systems.

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

The implementation of cooperation as referred to in Article 21 is in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VI
CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

PREVENTION OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 24

1. To prevent acts of violence against women and children, the Regional Government conducts socialization, empowerment, and awareness-raising to families, parents, and the community by providing information, guidance and/or counseling.
2. In addition to empowerment and awareness-raising as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government undertakes the following efforts:
a. increasing the quantity and quality of education both formal and non-formal and informal;
b. opening employment opportunities for women;
c. building community participation and concern for the prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence; and
d. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care about women and children.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 25

1. Control, guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be carried out by the Regent, the implementation of which shall be carried out by the Vice Regent.
2. The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out on a daily basis by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

FINANCING

Article 26

All activities related to the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

REPORTING

Article 27

1. The Head of the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection affairs shall report periodically to the Regent on the implementation of this Regional Regulation.
2. The reporting procedure as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 28

1. At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to and/or have not been replaced by new regulations.
2. The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency that has been established prior to the enactment of this Regional Regulation shall remain recognized for its existence.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 29

Matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation insofar as concerning its implementation shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.

translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF OGAN KOMERING ULU REGENCY

NUMBER 6 OF 2012 CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN.

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF OGAN KOMERING ULU REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Gender-based violence and violence against children is a social phenomenon that has existed since ancient times and has become increasingly prevalent recently. In fact, gender-based violence and violence against children continues to increase, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, trafficking of women and children, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, exploitation of migrant workers, and neglect, will apparently continue to be encountered in daily life, both in the domestic (household) and public spheres.

The causal factors of gender-based violence and violence against children are very complex and interrelated with one another. These factors include, among others, legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the concept that women and children are family property (assets), media that do not support reporting on violence against women and children, public services that are not yet optimal, customs that sometimes legalize violence, poverty issues, erroneous interpretations of religious teachings, all of which are wrapped in patriarchal culture.

The handling of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children occurring in Ogan Komering Ulu Regency, in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, requires that Regional Governments establish and develop a system and mechanism of cooperation for handling violence. Furthermore, based on the provisions of Article 26 paragraph (1) letter b of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government, it states that the Deputy Regional Head has the duty to assist the Regional Head in coordinating the activities of vertical agencies in the region, following up on reports and/or findings of supervisory apparatus oversight, implementing women's and youth empowerment, as well as seeking the development and preservation of socio-culture and the environment. Thus it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF OGAN KOMERING ULU REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

Point a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Point b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, compatible and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in community, national and state life.

Point d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Point e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.

Point f What is meant by child "growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.

What is meant by child "survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.

Point g What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Point h What is meant by "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers and KPK2BGA.

Point i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious leaders, social workers, police.

Point j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.

Point k What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen the victim, whether physically, psychologically, socially or economically.

Point l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the victim.

Point m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.
